I will keep the farm split between millet and soybean instead of pushing everything into one crop. I have 220.1 mu, only five years of farming experience, and a household of four, so I want a plan that is manageable, diversified, and not too dependent on one market or one weather outcome. Because I have well irrigation, I will use it strategically rather than heavily. Millet is naturally more drought-tolerant, so I will keep irrigation and fertilizer moderate there. Soybean fits my system well, helps with field balance, and needs less nitrogen, so I will rely more on phosphorus and potassium to support rooting and pod filling. I will use improved seed on soybean for stable emergence and hybrid seed on millet for stronger yield potential. I will plough before sowing because at the start of the season I want a clean, even seedbed and good early establishment. I will keep pesticide use limited but not zero, because I would rather intervene on time than risk stand loss or yield loss later. My goal is stable production across both crops, not the highest-risk maximum yield.
